justification: All nine stated claims were independently tested on the same 17 genomes and all agree quantitatively or within the paper’s stated ranges. Central results replicate tightly: two clades with inter-clade ANI min 90.67% (~90.7%), the 12-genome split of 4 F. magna + 8 F. nericia matches exactly, and the core proteome is near-identical (1209 vs 1202). Remaining claims (genome stats, open/heterogeneous pangenome, CAMP copy number, and virulence-factor heterogeneity including protein L at 11% vs ~10%) are confirmed; the main gaps are that Parsnp core-SNP phylogeny/BRIG and detailed pilus phylogeny were not regenerated, though functional conclusions were broadly supported by homology/annotation.
key_matches: C3: Two clades recovered; inter-clade ANI min 90.67% vs paper 90.7% (range 90.67–91.70%); intra-clade ANI mean 96.06%
C5: Core proteome 1209 families in all 12 vs paper 1202; core fraction 69.9% vs 68%
C2: Genome stats closely match (mean CDS 1759 vs 1760; GC 31.7–32.1%; size 1679–2033 kb)
C9: Protein L detected 2/17 (11%), matching paper’s ~10%; other host-interacting factors heterogeneous (e.g., PAB 8/17, FAF 12/17)
gaps: Parsnp core-SNP tree (126,647 SNPs) and BRIG comparative genomics figures were not reproduced with an equivalent SNP-based pipeline
Pilus locus conservation (C7) was supported broadly, but Fmp1 presence was partly annotation-limited and not validated with a dedicated locus/phylogeny reconstruction
